designPrinciple: Platform understanding precedes abstraction; every important concept moves quickly from explanation to browser observation, implementation, deliberate failure, debugging, testing, and explanation.
targetLearner: Complete beginner with basic computer literacy only

resourceRoleStrategy.reference: Optional precision consultation; never the sole source of assessed knowledge.

progressionPolicy: Weeks 9–19 retain checkpoints while increasing learner decisions.
Weeks 20–27 require architecture and testing decisions inside React.
Weeks 28–33 resemble ticket, release, and capstone work with review gates.
workloadPrinciples: Resource time includes active pauses and examples.
Most time is reserved for Studio, Build, debugging, testing, proof, and explanation.
Duration is the sum of authored workload.
assessmentPolicy: Every Week maps ten distinct knowledge/reasoning targets because the current runtime requires ten questions; practical competence remains proven by Studio, Builds, Projects, and Proof.

projectArchitecture.title: Accessible Responsive Site
projectArchitecture.outcome: Create a semantic, accessible, responsive multi-page site from content structure through viewport verification.

projectArchitecture.title: Vanilla JavaScript Product
projectArchitecture.outcome: Build a modular, resilient browser application that consumes an API without framework abstractions.

projectArchitecture.title: Typed and Tested Workflow
projectArchitecture.outcome: Move a real frontend project through Git review, modern tooling, TypeScript boundaries, and automated tests.

projectArchitecture.title: Production React Application
projectArchitecture.outcome: Build, test, harden, deploy, and deliver a routed React product feature through a professional workflow.

projectArchitecture.title: Independent Frontend Capstone
projectArchitecture.outcome: Frame, build, validate, release, and defend an independent production-quality frontend application.
